title: Cypriot, a language without its own name
text:
The people of the island speak a language of their own. Nobody in the harbor can tell you what they call it; the name by which they knew it is not written anywhere that can still be read, so the tablet and this page call it Cypriot.

Its signs are cut into clay and stone in a script no one here can read aloud. Learning the speech opens the yard and the smithy; it does not open the writing.

provenance.notes: The language and script are attested. The loss of the language’s own name and the undeciphered script are the reason the interface uses a modern label.
